name: Misoprostol
route_note: Oral tablets; also used buccally, sublingually or vaginally in obstetric and gynaecological regimens

discovery.note: A synthetic, orally active and more stable analogue of prostaglandin E1.

tagline: Prostaglandin analogue for NSAID ulcers, obstetric haemorrhage and abortion care
summary: Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin E1 analogue approved to prevent NSAID-induced gastric ulcers. Its uterotonic and cervical-ripening effects make it central to medical abortion, management of miscarriage, labour induction and postpartum haemorrhage, uses endorsed by WHO.
mechanism: In the stomach, misoprostol acid binds prostaglandin EP3 receptors on parietal cells, reducing acid secretion, and stimulates mucus and bicarbonate secretion and mucosal blood flow, protecting against NSAID injury.

In the uterus, activation of EP receptors increases myometrial contractions and softens the cervix. Combined with mifepristone, which blocks progesterone, it terminates early pregnancy with high efficacy.
uses: Prevention of NSAID-induced gastric ulcers (labelled US indication)
Medical abortion with mifepristone (labelled in many countries)
Labour induction (approved formulations in some countries)
Prevention and treatment of postpartum haemorrhage
Management of incomplete abortion and miscarriage

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: FDA approves Cytotec to prevent NSAID-induced gastric ulcers.

history.title: Medical abortion
history.detail: FDA approves mifepristone, with labelled regimen including misoprostol.

history.title: Postpartum haemorrhage
history.detail: WHO adds misoprostol to the Model List for prevention of postpartum haemorrhage.

history.title: US regimen update
history.detail: FDA updates the mifepristone label to a regimen using buccal misoprostol up to 70 days' gestation.

history.title: WHO guidance
history.detail: WHO abortion care guideline includes misoprostol-only regimens where mifepristone is unavailable.

pk.bioavailability: Rapidly absorbed and de-esterified; extensive first pass
pk.metabolism: De-esterification to active misoprostol acid, then fatty-acid oxidation

serious: Uterine rupture, particularly with prior caesarean scar
Abortion, premature birth or birth defects if taken in pregnancy for ulcer prevention
safety.boxed_warning: Can cause abortion, premature birth or birth defects; uterine rupture reported when used in pregnancy; not to be used by pregnant women to reduce NSAID ulcer risk.

facts: Misoprostol is heat-stable, which makes it practical for obstetric use in low-resource settings.
It is listed on the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines for reproductive health uses.
